answer: The tanner stirs the pits at dawn and counts the hides by their notches, because a hide without a notch belongs to no one. School governor appointment with education authority attestation is the notch: four-year appointment, meeting attendance record, training, registry entry. The kernel is one hide, soaked and scraped by hands that know the bark liquor. A forged notch is spotted when the hide is stretched, and the timber is the forfeit, two years of pit fees paid to the guild and the yard shut for a season. The pulse is the guild register, entered by the master tanner and open to any buyer.
